title: IAM Identity Center: one sign-in for many accounts

kcs.statement: IAM Identity Center (formerly AWS Single Sign-On) gives workforce users one sign-in portal for all the AWS accounts in an organization and for supported business applications.
IAM Identity Center grants access by assigning a user or group a permission set in a chosen account. The permission set becomes an IAM role in that account.
IAM Identity Center can use its own built-in directory, an external identity provider such as Okta or Microsoft Entra ID, or a Microsoft Active Directory as its source of identities.

problem_ideas: Auditors need read-only access to 25 accounts. Design the permission set and group assignment.
A company already uses Okta for 800 staff. Which identity source should Identity Center use?
Choose between IAM Identity Center and creating IAM users in each of 15 accounts for the same 50 engineers, and count the credentials each option creates.
What does a developer see after signing in to the Identity Center access portal?
A permission set is changed from ReadOnly to PowerUser. Which accounts' roles are updated?
Scenario: a question says 'centrally manage workforce access to multiple AWS accounts'. Name the service and the closest distractor.
